title: Sources of Real Estate Law & the Court System
originality: All items original to LicensePath. Modeled on the DRE exam blueprint and style only; no actual exam items reproduced.

questions.stem: A statute is a law enacted by:
rationales: HOAs make private rules, not statutes.

questions.stem: A regulation is generally adopted by:
rationales: Correct. Agencies adopt regulations under delegated authority.

questions.stem: A lease clause conflicts with applicable housing law. Which normally controls?
rationales: Private agreements cannot authorize prohibited conduct.
Correct. Higher applicable law controls conflicting private terms.
An agent opinion is not controlling law.

questions.stem: A city zoning rule is usually an:
rationales: Correct. Cities and counties adopt local ordinances.
Federal statutes are enacted by Congress.
A deed is private property instrument.

questions.stem: A client asks whether an easement permits a gate. The agent should:
options: Identify issue and refer to title or qualified counsel
rationales: Legal interpretation can exceed the licensee role.
Correct. The agent may identify and route the issue.
Correct. Courts develop case law through decisions.
Advertising rules may be statutes or regulations.

questions.stem: Why should an agent avoid treating a case headline as a universal rule?
options: Facts, court, and later authority may differ
Cases never apply to real estate
rationales: Correct. Legal effect depends on authority, facts, and currency.
Headlines can be accurate but incomplete.
Cases often apply to real estate.

questions.stem: The California trial court that hears many civil real-estate disputes is the:
rationales: Correct. Superior Courts are California trial courts.
DRE is an agency, not a civil trial court.

questions.stem: A brokerage receives a regulatory request for ad records. A salesperson should:
rationales: Correct. Preserve facts and use the brokerage response process.

questions.stem: A neighbor's short-term rental listing is proof that a buyer may do the same. This is:
options: False; local, HOA, loan, and property facts must be verified
rationales: A neighbor's conduct is not authority.
Correct. Multiple current rules and documents may apply.
Financing does not make conduct lawful.
Agent opinion cannot substitute for authority.

questions.stem: A preliminary title report should prompt an agent to:
options: Identify questions and seek qualified review
rationales: Legal interpretation may exceed the role.
Correct. Identify issues and route them properly.
Agents cannot guarantee a title product.

options: Authority over a subject, person, or area
Higher law displacing conflicting lower law
rationales: Correct. Preemption concerns conflict between levels of law.

questions.stem: The best response to a legal-looking question is usually to:
options: Preserve facts, state boundaries, and refer appropriately
rationales: Correct. This is the professional legal-risk workflow.

questions.stem: An agency handbook is best treated as:
options: Useful guidance whose current authority must be checked
rationales: Correct. Guidance can be useful but must be distinguished from binding authority.
Guidance is not necessarily a private contract.

questions.stem: An HOA rule may be important, but an agent should not say it overrides:
rationales: Correct. Private rules must remain consistent with applicable higher law.
